name: Value Proposition Canvas Customer Profiling
phase: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [customer segment] considers [pain point Y] significantly more critical than [pain point Z]. We will verify this by conducting 10 canvas alignment exercises, and consider it validated if ≥ 75% of participants independently cluster their top 3 jobs and pains into identical operational nodes.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Lay out an empty customer profile of jobs, pains and gains on a board that participants can move.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Run an unmoderated card sort into functional, social and emotional categories, then rank pains and gains.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Record where items cluster and correlate the rankings across participants.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Construct an unpopulated Value Proposition Canvas Customer Profile (comprising Jobs, Pains, and Gains) using standardized markdown or digital boards.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Guide users through an unmoderated card-sort protocol. Instruct them to place operational responsibilities into functional, social, and emotional categories, then rank pains by severity and gains by relevance.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Record the spatial clustering of items. Calculate Spearman rank-order correlation coefficients across participant cards.

warning.label: Aspirational Self-Deception
warning.text: People elevate noble social and emotional jobs above the mundane functional tasks that decide the purchase.

warningFull: Participants consistently overemphasize noble emotional or social jobs while minimizing the mundane, repetitive functional tasks that dictate enterprise purchase behavior.

origin.title: Value Proposition Design: How to Create Products and Services Customers Want
